boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Emerson College
boards.description: Ten under-21-safe food, dessert, and supply stops with documented late hours, ranging from Emerson’s own campus market to nearby Theatre District and Boston destinations.

cards.title: Tacos Until 2 A.M.
cards.subtitle: 80 Boylston Street, beside Emerson’s Boston campus
cards.notes: Check the live location hours, then walk to the Boylston Street storefront for tacos, burritos, bowls, or a late dinner to go.
cards.short_summary: A campus-edge taqueria with documented service until 2 a.m. every day.
cards.evidence_claim: El Jefe’s official website lists its Boston Common restaurant at 80 Boylston Street and states that it operates daily from 8 a.m. to 2 a.m.
cards.source_title: El Jefe’s Taqueria | Authentic Mexican Food. Open Til 4AM.
cards.access_notes: The official location listing shows 8 a.m.–2 a.m. seven days a week; confirm same-day service before leaving campus.

cards.title: The Tremont Street Pizza Window
cards.subtitle: 224 Tremont Street in the Theatre District
cards.notes: Walk down Tremont Street and consult the day-specific schedule before ordering; Thursday through Saturday carry the latest posted closing.
cards.short_summary: A nearby pizzeria whose official schedule extends to 3 a.m. on three nights.
cards.evidence_claim: New York Pizza’s official Theatre District page lists 224 Tremont Street and hours until 1 a.m. Sunday through Wednesday and 3 a.m. Thursday through Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Official hours run to 1 a.m. Sunday–Wednesday and 3 a.m. Thursday–Saturday; check for holiday changes.

cards.title: Dumplings After Midnight
cards.subtitle: 695 Washington Street in Chinatown
cards.notes: Continue toward Chinatown and check the official schedule first; Friday and Saturday offer the latest documented ordering window.
cards.short_summary: A Chinatown dumpling destination with weekend hours extending past 1 a.m.
cards.evidence_claim: Dumpling Cafe’s direct ordering site identifies the restaurant at 695 Washington Street and lists Friday and Saturday service until 1:30 a.m.
cards.source_title: Dumpling Cafe - Boston | Location and Hours
cards.access_notes: The direct location page lists 11 a.m.–1:30 a.m. Friday and Saturday and 11 or 11:30 p.m. closings on other nights.

cards.title: The All-Night Diner Run
cards.subtitle: 178 Kneeland Street near South Station
cards.notes: Use well-lit main streets toward Kneeland Street, verify conditions before departing, and choose the diner when other kitchens have closed.
cards.short_summary: A classic diner whose own site explicitly documents continuous 24/7 operation.
cards.evidence_claim: South Street Diner’s official late-night page gives its address as 178 Kneeland Street and states that it is open 24 hours a day, seven days a week.
cards.source_title: South Street Diner - Boston’s Only Late Night Eats
cards.access_notes: The restaurant’s official page states that it is open 24/7; verify weather and walking conditions before making the trip.

cards.title: A South End Kebab Run
cards.subtitle: 145 East Berkeley Street in the South End
cards.notes: Check the restaurant’s live ordering status, then head southwest for Turkish and Middle Eastern takeout during its posted late window.
cards.short_summary: A South End restaurant with takeout hours documented through 2 a.m.
cards.evidence_claim: Ali Baba’s direct location and ordering page lists 145 East Berkeley Street and takeout service until 2 a.m. on its posted schedule.
cards.source_title: Ali Baba Locations | Pickup or Delivery Available
cards.access_notes: The direct ordering page posts takeout through 2 a.m.; use its live open/closed indicator to confirm service before traveling.

cards.title: Burgers on Dartmouth Street
cards.subtitle: 145 Dartmouth Street near Back Bay Station
cards.notes: Check the official day-specific schedule and take Boylston Street west; Friday and Saturday extend two hours beyond the weekday close.
cards.short_summary: A Back Bay burger counter open until midnight or later throughout the week.
cards.evidence_claim: Tasty Burger’s official Back Bay page lists 145 Dartmouth Street and hours until midnight Sunday through Thursday and 2 a.m. Friday and Saturday.
cards.source_title: Back Bay | Hours + Location | Tasty Burger
cards.access_notes: Official hours are 11 a.m.–midnight Sunday–Thursday and 11 a.m.–2 a.m. Friday–Saturday; confirm before departure.

cards.title: Cookies on Clarendon Street
cards.subtitle: 222 Clarendon Street in Back Bay
cards.notes: Head toward Clarendon Street for a dessert-focused run, checking the bakery’s ordering page for live availability before setting out.
cards.short_summary: A late-night bakery documented through midnight or 1 a.m., depending on the day.
cards.evidence_claim: Insomnia Cookies’ official Back Bay announcement identifies 222 Clarendon Street and lists midnight closings Sunday through Wednesday and 1 a.m. Thursday through Saturday.
cards.source_title: Insomnia Cookies Opens Fourth Boston Location
cards.access_notes: The official store announcement posts midnight closings Sunday–Wednesday and 1 a.m. Thursday–Saturday; recheck live ordering hours.

cards.title: A Round-the-Clock Bakery
cards.subtitle: 134 Salem Street in the North End
cards.notes: Plan the longer North End trip with a companion, use main streets, and confirm conditions even though the bakery documents continuous operation.
cards.short_summary: A named North End bakery whose official history page states it never closes.
cards.evidence_claim: Bova’s Bakery’s official site gives its address as 134 Salem Street and states that the family bakery is open 24 hours a day, every day.
cards.access_notes: The bakery’s official page states it is open 24 hours every day; account for the longer walk from Emerson and verify conditions.

cards.title: The On-Campus 2 A.M. Option
cards.subtitle: Inside Piano Row on Emerson’s Boston campus
cards.notes: Use this campus stop for snacks, groceries, coffee, or grill items; check Emerson dining notices because academic breaks can alter access.
cards.short_summary: Emerson’s own convenience market, with a recent college notice identifying 2 a.m. as its normal close.
cards.evidence_claim: Emerson identifies C-Store at the Max as a market and café inside Piano Row, while a January 2026 college notice gives normal Max Cafe hours as 11 a.m. to 2 a.m.
cards.source_title: Winter Storm; Tuesday Schedule Changes for Boston Campus
cards.access_notes: Emerson’s January 2026 notice identifies normal Max Cafe hours as 11 a.m.–2 a.m.; campus access and break schedules may differ.

cards.title: The 24-Hour Supply Run
cards.subtitle: 587 Boylston Street near Copley Square
cards.notes: Use the retail store for packaged food or practical supplies, and note that its pharmacy counter follows shorter hours than the main store.
cards.short_summary: A Boylston Street retail stop whose store and photo departments operate continuously.
cards.evidence_claim: CVS’s official Boston locator lists the store at 587 Boylston Street and marks its store and photo services as open 24 hours.
cards.source_title: CVS Pharmacy Locations in Boston, Massachusetts
cards.access_notes: The official CVS locator marks the store and photo department open 24 hours; the pharmacy counter closes earlier and has separate hours.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten Emerson spaces for studying, meeting, creating, playing, reflecting, and exercising, with uses and access conditions verified through current college sources.

cards.title: Reset Between Classes at Griff’s
cards.subtitle: Games and soft seating on Little Building’s second floor
cards.notes: Bring friends for pool, air hockey, foosball, arcade, Switch, or tabletop games; keep food and drinks at the room’s regular tables.
cards.short_summary: A nonreservable campus third space dedicated to casual play and downtime.
cards.evidence_claim: Emerson identifies Griff’s Game Room as a second-floor Little Building space where students can play games, relax, and connect during operating hours.
cards.access_notes: Open to Emerson students and community members during posted operational hours. Outside guests need an active Emerson sponsor and visitor registration.

cards.title: Take a Common-Facing Work Break
cards.subtitle: The main-level community lounge at 172 Tremont
cards.notes: Use The Hub for an informal study session or meetup, then ask the nearby Campus Centers service desk if you need reservable space.
cards.short_summary: A community lounge for low-setup studying and conversation.
cards.evidence_claim: Emerson lists The Hub as the main-level community lounge within 172 Tremont, a building offering student meeting and social spaces.
cards.access_notes: For Emerson community use; room reservations and access assistance are available through the 172 Tremont service desk.

cards.title: Prep a Meal While You Meet
cards.subtitle: A shared kitchen for casual gathering at 172 Tremont
cards.notes: Plan a small meal-prep meetup here and check with Campus Centers before treating the kitchen as event space or assuming exclusive use.
cards.short_summary: A practical shared kitchen that doubles as a casual gathering place.
cards.evidence_claim: Emerson describes the Community Kitchen at 172 Tremont as a space for casual gathering, meal preparation, and limited events.
cards.access_notes: Located inside 172 Tremont for the Emerson community. Limited events or reserved uses should be coordinated with Campus Centers.

cards.title: Give the Group a Formal Home Base
cards.subtitle: A presentation and workshop room at 172 Tremont
cards.notes: Request this room when your group needs a defined setting for a presentation, workshop, event, or structured meeting rather than a lounge.
cards.short_summary: A reservable multipurpose setting for organized group work.
cards.evidence_claim: Emerson identifies the Owens Multipurpose Room at 172 Tremont as a space for formal meetings, presentations, workshops, and events.
cards.access_notes: Campus Center spaces can be requested through Spacebook; the 172 Tremont service desk can assist with booking and access.

cards.title: Find the Fourth-Floor Cultural Hub
cards.subtitle: Community space inside 172 Tremont
cards.notes: Go to the fourth floor for the Cultural Engagement Center, and consult its staff or posted programming before planning a group visit.
cards.short_summary: A specifically named cultural-engagement space within a central student building.
cards.evidence_claim: Emerson’s current 172 Tremont page locates the Cultural Engagement Center on the building’s fourth floor.
cards.access_notes: Located on the fourth floor of 172 Tremont. Program participation and room access may depend on the Center’s current schedule.

cards.title: Make Room for Reflection
cards.subtitle: Emerson’s multifaith hub at 172 Tremont
cards.notes: Use the Center’s fourth-floor setting for spiritual support or reflection; respect prayer areas and check current programming before arriving.
cards.short_summary: An inclusive multifaith campus hub with dedicated reflection facilities.
cards.evidence_claim: Emerson identifies the Center for Spiritual Life as its inclusive multifaith hub and locates it on 172 Tremont’s fourth floor with prayer and ablution space.
cards.access_notes: Campus resource for Emerson students; specific programs, support, and prayer-space use may follow posted schedules or Center guidance.

cards.title: Switch to a Quieter Setting
cards.subtitle: A focused lounge inside the Max Mutchnick Campus Center
cards.notes: Head to Piano Row’s second-floor campus center when conversation-heavy lounges are not working, and preserve the room’s quiet purpose.
cards.short_summary: A named campus-center lounge intended for quieter use.
cards.evidence_claim: Emerson states that the second-floor Max Mutchnick Campus Center in Piano Row houses the Quiet Lounge.
cards.access_notes: Located within the Max Mutchnick Campus Center on Piano Row’s second floor; access follows campus-building operations.

cards.title: Reserve a Room Beyond the Classroom
cards.subtitle: A managed gathering space in Piano Row
cards.notes: Consider the Beard Room for an organized meeting or event, then request it through Spacebook instead of assuming walk-in availability.
cards.short_summary: A named campus-center room available through Emerson’s reservation system.
cards.evidence_claim: Emerson lists the Beard Room inside the Max Mutchnick Campus Center and identifies it as a campus space managed by Business Services.
cards.access_notes: The Emerson community may request campus rooms through Spacebook. A reservation does not imply unrestricted public access.

cards.title: Book the Library Room Before the Meeting
cards.subtitle: Reservable study rooms managed by Iwasaki Library
cards.notes: Request a study room for focused individual or group work, and arrive on time so the space can serve the reservation as planned.
cards.short_summary: Library-managed rooms that give collaborative work a defined boundary.
cards.evidence_claim: Emerson’s current space-management directory specifically lists Library Study Rooms and CoLab as spaces managed by Iwasaki Library.
cards.access_notes: Study-room use is managed by Iwasaki Library; confirm current availability and reservation requirements with the Library.

cards.title: Use the Lab That Stays Class-Free
cards.subtitle: Mac workstations and printers in Little Building 230
cards.notes: Bring computer-based work to Little Building 230 when you need a Mac or printer; verify current lab hours before making the trip.
cards.short_summary: An open-access computer lab designed for work outside scheduled classes.
cards.evidence_claim: Emerson Technology lists SBL in Little Building 230 as an open-access lab for students, faculty, and staff, with 15 Mac workstations and printers.
cards.source_title: Lab and kiosk locations and resources
cards.access_notes: Available to Emerson students, faculty, and staff during lab operating hours. Check the current technology schedule before visiting.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten documented no-admission, no-purchase activities for Emerson students around Boston.

cards.title: See an ArtsEmerson performance
cards.subtitle: ArtsEmerson venues, downtown Boston
cards.notes: Bring a valid Emerson ID to the box office on the performance day, then ask whether a free student ticket remains for that in-person show.
cards.short_summary: A same-day, ID-based way for Emerson students to attend an ArtsEmerson show without buying a ticket.
cards.evidence_claim: Emerson students, faculty, and staff may receive one free ticket to an in-person ArtsEmerson theatre performance, film screening, or concert by presenting valid Emerson ID at the box office on the day of the event.
cards.source_title: Free/Low-Cost Resources for Students | Emerson College
cards.access_notes: Emerson ID is required; availability is determined at the box office on the event day.

cards.title: Join a library class or program
cards.subtitle: Central Library in Copley Square
cards.notes: Check BPL’s calendar, choose a no-cost class or program, and meet friends in the public library instead of planning a purchase-based outing.
cards.short_summary: Boston Public Library offers public learning and event options at no cost.
cards.evidence_claim: Emerson’s student-resources page states that Boston Public Library offers events, contests, classes, and training at no cost.
cards.source_title: Free/Low-Cost Resources for Students | Emerson College
cards.access_notes: Use the BPL calendar to confirm the individual program’s date and capacity.

cards.title: Browse a free map exhibition
cards.subtitle: Boston Public Library, Central Library
cards.notes: Walk through the exhibition cases together and compare historic maps or printed materials; the library identifies its exhibitions as free and public.
cards.short_summary: A public exhibition stop inside Boston Public Library’s Central Library.
cards.evidence_claim: Boston Public Library’s exhibition procedures require all exhibitions to be free of charge and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Central Library—Copley Square Exhibition Procedures | Boston Public Library
cards.access_notes: Check current exhibitions before visiting; standard library building access rules apply.

cards.title: Look through contemporary art galleries
cards.subtitle: 20 Ames Street, Cambridge
cards.notes: Meet at the List Center, move through the galleries at your own pace, and use the free digital guide if you want prompts for discussion.
cards.short_summary: MIT’s contemporary-art galleries welcome all visitors without admission.
cards.evidence_claim: The MIT List Visual Arts Center states that it is free and open to all.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit | MIT List Visual Arts Center
cards.access_notes: The official visitor page lists gallery hours and visitor policies; verify hours before travel.

cards.entity_name: MIT Museum Studio and Compton Gallery
cards.title: See a changing MIT exhibition
cards.subtitle: MIT Building 10, Room 150, Cambridge
cards.notes: Use the free gallery as a compact meet-up: view the changing exhibition, then spend a few minutes comparing one work or idea each.
cards.short_summary: A free changing-exhibition space on MIT’s campus.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT Arts lists the MIT Museum Studio and Compton Gallery as open daily with free admission.
cards.access_notes: MIT lists it as open daily, 10:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.; confirm access before going.

cards.title: Take in architecture-school gallery work
cards.subtitle: MIT Building 7, Room 408, Cambridge
cards.notes: Plan a short gallery stop with friends and use the surrounding common areas for conversation after viewing the current display.
cards.short_summary: A free MIT gallery near architecture studios and lecture spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT Arts lists Keller Gallery in Building 7, Room 408, with free admission.
cards.access_notes: MIT lists hours as Monday–Sunday, 9:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m.; verify before travel.

cards.title: Explore biomedical images and research
cards.subtitle: MIT Koch Institute, Cambridge
cards.notes: Visit the public galleries together, read the project displays, and pick one image or research question to discuss on the way out.
cards.short_summary: MIT’s public galleries connect visitors with biomedical images and cancer-research projects.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT Arts describes the Koch Institute Public Galleries as spaces for visitors to explore current cancer research, biomedical images, and related contexts; its exhibitions page identifies the gallery offerings as free admission.
cards.access_notes: Review MIT’s current exhibition information before visiting campus.

cards.title: Reserve a free MAAM visit
cards.subtitle: 621 Huntington Avenue, Boston
cards.notes: Reserve a no-cost timed ticket, then use the gallery visit as a focused afternoon activity with time afterward to talk about the work.
cards.short_summary: MassArt’s teaching museum presents contemporary art with free admission.
cards.evidence_claim: MassArt Art Museum states that it is always free and offers free tickets for visits.
cards.access_notes: Advance ticket registration is recommended; the museum notes that tickets can sell out.

cards.title: Take a self-guided plant walk
cards.subtitle: 125 Arborway, Boston
cards.notes: Choose a self-guided tour from the Arboretum’s visitor page, walk the marked landscape together, and stay on paths while observing plants and wildlife.
cards.short_summary: A large living collection with free daily landscape access and self-guided routes.
cards.evidence_claim: The Arnold Arboretum states that its 281-acre landscape is open daily and free for all to explore, with admission always free.
cards.source_title: Visit | Arnold Arboretum of Harvard University
cards.access_notes: Landscape access is daily from sunrise to sunset; follow posted visitor guidelines.

cards.title: Board USS Constitution
cards.subtitle: Charlestown Navy Yard, Boston
cards.notes: Bring required government photo ID if 18 or older, allow time for security screening, and board on a first-come basis during ship visiting hours.
cards.short_summary: A free, first-come visit aboard the active historic Navy ship.
cards.evidence_claim: USS Constitution Museum states that the ship is free to visit on a first-come, first-served basis.
cards.access_notes: The ship is open Wednesday–Sunday, 10:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m.; security screening is required, and visitors 18+ need federal or state photo ID.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Named public-facing destinations along the Tremont, Park, Beacon, Arlington, and Washington Street corridors surrounding Emerson’s downtown campus.

cards.title: Boston Common
cards.subtitle: Tremont Street corridor
cards.notes: Enter from Tremont Street and use the shaded paths to connect campus to lawns, ball fields, the playground, and the Frog Pond.
cards.short_summary: A historic civic landscape with several outdoor recreation features.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service identifies Boston Common at 148 Tremont Street and notes its ball fields, playground, Frog Pond, tennis courts, and open space.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public park; check City of Boston notices for event-related access changes.

cards.title: Boston Common Frog Pond
cards.subtitle: Tremont Street corridor, inside Boston Common
cards.notes: Check the seasonal program before heading over; winter operations include public skating, rentals, concessions, restrooms, and a warming area.
cards.short_summary: A seasonal Common destination centered on winter skating.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Boston states that the Frog Pond offers public skating in winter and lists skate rentals, restrooms, concessions, and a warming area.
cards.access_notes: Seasonal: the City says skating runs November through March; rentals and skating involve charges.

cards.title: Granary Burying Ground
cards.subtitle: Tremont Street corridor, between Park and School Streets
cards.notes: Walk the marked paths and look for the memorials to Samuel Adams, John Hancock, Paul Revere, and Boston Massacre victims.
cards.short_summary: A city-managed historic burying ground with Revolutionary-era figures.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Boston places Granary Burying Ground on Tremont Street between Park and School Streets and documents graves of Adams, Hancock, Revere, and Boston Massacre victims.
cards.access_notes: Historic outdoor site; use the City’s site maps and follow posted preservation guidance.

cards.title: Park Street Church
cards.subtitle: Park Street corridor beside Boston Common
cards.notes: See the Freedom Trail exhibit for the building’s abolitionist-era and civic history, then take in the view across the Common.
cards.short_summary: A Freedom Trail church with a current free historic exhibit.
cards.evidence_claim: Park Street Church says it stands on Boston Common, is a Freedom Trail stop, and offers a free immersive exhibit Monday through Saturday.
cards.access_notes: The church lists exhibit hours Monday–Saturday, 9:30 a.m.–3 p.m.; hours are subject to change.

cards.title: King's Chapel Burying Ground
cards.subtitle: Tremont Street corridor, between School and Park Streets
cards.notes: Pause at the city’s oldest burying place and use the site’s names to orient a compact walk through early Boston history.
cards.short_summary: Boston Proper’s oldest burying place on the Tremont Street corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Boston identifies King’s Chapel Burying Ground on Tremont Street between School and Park Streets and dates its founding to 1630.
cards.access_notes: Historic outdoor site; follow posted access and preservation rules.

cards.title: Massachusetts State House
cards.subtitle: Beacon Street corridor
cards.notes: Use the official visitor information to plan a civic-history stop at the state capitol and confirm entry procedures before arrival.
cards.short_summary: The Commonwealth’s active capitol, museum of art and history, and public gathering site.
cards.evidence_claim: Mass.gov describes the State House as a place for government and business, a museum of art and history, and a site for public congregation at 24 Beacon Street.
cards.access_notes: Visitor screening and building access procedures apply; the accessible entrance and RIDE drop-off are on Bowdoin Street.

cards.title: Boston Athenaeum
cards.subtitle: Beacon Street corridor, near Park Street
cards.notes: Browse the first-floor installations or book ahead for a tour; research appointments are available for working with special collections.
cards.short_summary: A Beacon Street cultural library with exhibitions, tours, and special-collections research.
cards.evidence_claim: The Boston Athenaeum lists rotating exhibitions, art and architecture tours, and free research appointments at 10½ Beacon Street.
cards.access_notes: First-floor admission and day memberships have fees; research appointments are free and should be arranged in advance.

cards.title: Boston Public Garden
cards.subtitle: Arlington and Charles Street corridors
cards.notes: Follow the curved paths around the pond to see the Victorian landscape, statuary, fountains, plantings, and Swan Boats area.
cards.short_summary: A landmark public botanical garden beside Boston Common.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service identifies the Boston Public Garden at 4 Charles Street as the first public botanical garden in the United States, with paths, statuary, fountains, and a pond.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public park; Swan Boat rides are a separate seasonal activity.

cards.title: Old South Meeting House
cards.subtitle: Washington Street corridor
cards.notes: Plan a museum stop around the 1729 meeting house and its Boston Tea Party interpretation; allow time for the current exhibits.
cards.short_summary: A Washington Street Freedom Trail museum in the 1729 meeting house.
cards.evidence_claim: Old South Meeting House identifies itself as the 1729 meeting house where the Boston Tea Party began and lists its Washington Street address and visitor hours.
cards.access_notes: The museum lists daily seasonal hours and paid admission for most visitors; verify holiday closures before going.

cards.title: Old State House
cards.subtitle: Washington Street corridor at State Street
cards.notes: Use the two exhibition floors to trace debates, people, and events that shaped Boston’s role before and during the Revolution.
cards.short_summary: A Washington Street museum devoted to Boston’s colonial and Revolutionary civic history.
cards.evidence_claim: The Old State House describes the building as Boston’s 18th-century civic center and says its two exhibition floors interpret Boston’s role in the American Revolution.
cards.access_notes: Museum admission is generally paid; confirm current hours and accessibility details before visiting.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Emerson College, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A Friday-to-Sunday sequence mixing Emerson gathering spaces, public art, nearby parks, local history, and a quiet library reset.

cards.title: Start at the Hub
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · 172 Tremont
cards.notes: Begin in the main-level Hub, then scan the building’s meeting spaces and student-organization offices for useful campus bearings.
cards.short_summary: Use Emerson’s collaboration center as your first social and practical campus anchor.
cards.evidence_claim: Emerson identifies 172 Tremont as a student collaboration destination with the Hub lounge, meeting spaces, and student-organization offices.
cards.access_notes: During primary academic semesters, weekend hours are 9:00 a.m.–10:00 p.m.; building access requirements may apply.

cards.title: See Moving-Image Art
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · 25 Avery Street
cards.notes: Walk through the current exhibition and notice how artists use video, performance, or emerging media before the gallery closes.
cards.short_summary: Open the weekend with a public contemporary-art stop embedded in Emerson’s campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Emerson Contemporary’s Media Art Gallery presents moving-image, performance, and emergent-media art; its programming is free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Open to the public Tuesday–Saturday, noon–6:00 p.m.; confirm the current exhibition before visiting.

cards.title: Settle In Over Dinner
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · 122 Boylston Street
cards.notes: Use dinner to compare weekend plans, then return any reusable Ozzi container to a designated cashier-station drop bin.
cards.short_summary: Make Emerson’s main dining hall the practical first-night meal stop.
cards.evidence_claim: The Dining Center at 122 Boylston Street is Emerson’s all-you-care-to-eat main dining hall with cooked-to-order and self-service stations.
cards.access_notes: Entry requires a meal swipe or payment by Board Bucks, ECCash, Visa, Mastercard, cash, credit, or debit; check the linked menu service for current hours.

cards.title: End Friday with a Game
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · Little Building
cards.notes: Head to the second floor of Little Building, choose an available game, and use the relaxed setting to learn a few classmates’ names.
cards.short_summary: Close the first day in an Emerson space designed for games and connection.
cards.evidence_claim: Emerson describes Griff’s Game Room on Little Building’s second floor as a place for students to play, connect, and relax.
cards.source_title: Student Engagement and Leadership (SEAL) — Emerson College
cards.access_notes: Student campus space; confirm access and posted operating hours before making it the evening stop.

cards.title: Take the Common Loop
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning · Across from campus
cards.notes: Begin near the Boylston Street edge and make a daylight walking loop past the Frog Pond, lawns, and Parkman Bandstand.
cards.short_summary: Get oriented to the historic public park directly facing Emerson’s campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Boston lists Boston Common as a municipal park with paths, the Frog Pond, athletic areas, fountains, and other public facilities.
cards.access_notes: Public outdoor park; visit in daylight, follow posted park rules, and do not enter or wade in the Frog Pond.

cards.title: Cross into the Garden
cards.subtitle: Saturday late morning · 4 Charles Street
cards.notes: Follow the meandering paths, cross the lagoon bridge, and photograph the seasonal plantings without stepping into garden beds.
cards.short_summary: Contrast the Common’s open grounds with Boston’s ornamental botanical garden.
cards.evidence_claim: Boston identifies the Public Garden as America’s first public botanical garden, with paths, a lagoon, monuments, fountains, and cultivated plantings.
cards.access_notes: Public outdoor garden at 4 Charles Street; Swan Boat rides are a separate seasonal paid activity.

cards.title: Reset in Copley Square
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · 700 Boylston Street
cards.notes: Enter through an accessible public entrance, ask the Welcome Center for a floor plan, and choose a reading area for a quiet reset.
cards.short_summary: Trade the busy downtown streets for public reading rooms, art, and architecture.
cards.evidence_claim: The Central Library at 700 Boylston Street offers public collections, Wi-Fi, computers, scanning, outdoor space, and accessible entrances.
cards.source_title: Central Library in Copley Square | Boston Public Library
cards.access_notes: Saturday hours are 9:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.; holiday closures and individual department hours may differ.

cards.title: Walk to Chinatown Gate
cards.subtitle: Saturday evening · Beach Street
cards.notes: Approach the gate from downtown, pause for a streetscape photo, then explore public blocks without treating the neighborhood as a backdrop.
cards.short_summary: Use a named civic landmark to begin a respectful walk through Chinatown.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Boston identifies the Chinatown Gate across Beach Street as the eastern entrance to the Chinatown neighborhood.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public landmark; remain on public sidewalks, respect residents and businesses, and use extra care after dark.

cards.title: Follow the Red Line
cards.subtitle: Sunday morning · Start at Boston Common
cards.notes: Begin at the Boston Common Visitor Information Center and follow a manageable section of the marked route with the official brochure.
cards.short_summary: Turn Sunday morning into a self-guided introduction to Boston’s historic core.
cards.evidence_claim: The Freedom Trail is a 2.5-mile red-lined route connecting 16 official historic sites, with visitor information available at Boston Common.
cards.access_notes: The outdoor route includes hills, brick, cobblestones, and uneven terrain; individual historic sites set their own admission and hours.

cards.title: Finish at the Paramount
cards.subtitle: Sunday afternoon · Washington Street
cards.notes: End outside the restored Art Deco façade and identify how the theater, rehearsal, production, and residential spaces share one complex.
cards.short_summary: Close the route at an Emerson landmark that joins performance, production, and campus life.
cards.evidence_claim: Emerson’s Paramount Center is a mixed-use performance and production complex containing theaters, rehearsal studios, a scene shop, movie studio, and residence hall.
